outputs.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE full-screen, beautifully art-directed PC game MAIN MENU screenshot for an original medieval adventure card game titled "FALL". Landscape 16:9, high resolution. This is a finished visual exploration, with original illustrations and designed game UI, not a website, wireframe, design board, or screenshot in a device.
Direction: THE CARD HALL. Take the structural lesson of GWENT/Faeria's illustrated activity cards, the heraldic material sophistication of Armello, and the quiet natural-light control of Anno. Create original art and interface, no copied characters or logos. The quality comes from composition, deliberate typography, richly painted narrative art, tactile restrained materials, and legible functional controls.

Composition: a coherent dim medieval council chamber is a subdued full-bleed backdrop, barely suggested stone arches, broad weathered oak foreground, cool window daylight. No candles or artificial lights. The overwhelmingly important central region is THREE distinct upright portrait activity cards, evenly spaced, all fully readable, with only slight dimensional depth and NO overlap. They occupy x=12–88%, y=18–68%. The middle card is about 8% taller and visibly selected. Never turn the cards into plain dashboard rectangles or placeholder icons.
Left card "THE TAVERN": beautifully painted close scene of two medieval travellers playing Spanish-suited cards across an oak table, muted warm leather and rust cloth, natural human proportions.
Middle card "CAMPAIGN": spectacular but believable original painting of a cloaked traveller on a winding road toward a fortified medieval city among layered blue-grey mountains; strong readable silhouette, cool sky, subtle ochre trees. Small readable chapter caption "CHAPTER II". This is the selected activity.
Right card "ARENA": imposing adult medieval champion in worn steel armour and burgundy cloth holding a small hand of cards, with a grounded stone tournament arcade behind; dignified, not a cartoon, no glowing weapons.
Each card has a crafted dark metal rim with small aged-brass corner inlays, fine engraved suit motifs (coin, sword, cup, club), a quiet solid lower title area, a prominent highly legible title, and just one short descriptor: left "A seat at the table", middle "The Borderlands", right "Prove your hand". Selection is a crisp ivory/brass rim and a tiny heraldic marker, not neon glow.

Header: visually quiet. Small circular painted player portrait top-left with "TRAVELLER" and "LEVEL 12" next to it. A modest elegant custom FALL wordmark at top centre. Top-right a compact coin icon with "1,240", then small mail and settings symbols; no large boxed dashboards.
Below selected centre card, a strong carefully designed oxblood button with fine brass edging, exact text "CONTINUE CAMPAIGN", visibly the primary action. Keep a clear gap between card and button. Small secondary "ALL MODES" with a modest chevron nearby on the right.
Lower-left, outside the cards, one restrained journal strip: quill/scroll emblem, "CURRENT QUEST", and "A debt at the crossroads". This is compact context, not a big panel.
Along bottom edge, a slim dark translucent engraved band with FIVE evenly spaced small illustrated metal emblems and clear text labels "HERO", "COLLECTION", "JOURNAL", "GUILD", "MARKET". Generous touchable spacing, understated compared to the primary action. The future systems make this read as a complete adventure game.

Typography: sophisticated engraved old-style serif labels, medium weight, tight well-kerned proportions, not thin widely spaced Roman capitals everywhere. Small utility text is a crisp readable humanist sans. Ivory main labels, muted warm-grey secondary type. Clear hierarchy at actual 16:9 screen size. Restrict gold to selective fine accents; no giant ornamental flourishes. Theme: near-black ink, slate blue, oxblood, aged brass, parchment. Rich nuanced original painterly artwork, disciplined value masses, selective fine details, matte natural materials.
Avoid: website navigation rail, marketing headline, hero CTA landing page, SaaS cards, placeholder artwork, flat geometric icons in the activity illustrations, excessive borders, gradients on every button, glows, candles, lanterns, flames, sunbursts, purple magical portals, cartoon trees, shiny plastic, anime, photoreal stock imagery, busy HUD, unreadable microtext, random badges, overlapping UI. All text and control positions must be plausible and aligned. No browser chrome, no annotation, no mockup title outside the game screen.

Use case: style-transfer / ui-mockup refinement.
EDIT THE PROVIDED FALL CARD HALL IMAGE. This is the approved composition and must remain recognisable. The user likes this exact three-activity main menu but wants less synthetic over-rendering and a simpler UI that can be built now. Retain its premium medieval card-game character. Produce ONE refined full-screen landscape mockup at the same 1672x941 aspect ratio.

INVARIANTS:
Keep the same layout and reading order: profile top left, FALL top centre, compact resources/mail/settings top right; three fully visible activity cards (Tavern left, selected Campaign centre, Arena right); the primary action immediately below Campaign; current-quest context bottom left, All Modes right; five evenly spaced destinations along the bottom. Keep the card sizes, relative positions, perspectives, and centre card slightly taller. Retain the SAME three illustration subjects and poses: two travellers playing cards at an oak table; cloaked traveller walking toward a mountain citadel; armoured champion holding cards. Same restrained daylight and cool slate/warm brown palette. Do not invent new subjects, architecture, features, or a fourth card. Do not turn this into a generic app or website.

REFINE THE ARTWORK:
Repaint with deliberate professional game-illustration simplification: cleaner silhouettes, organised large value shapes, controlled brush strokes, selective detail where it matters. Reduce tiny cracks, mottled speckles, scratches on every surface, repetitive castle micro-windows, individual hair strands, tiny foliage noise and waxy photorealistic face rendering. Keep mature natural human proportions, character identity and anatomy; no cartoon heads, cel-shaded anime, low-poly or flat vector style. Armour should be matte steel with a few designed highlights rather than a maze of bright scratches. Cloth has broad readable folds. Background castle has a strong designed silhouette and plausible grounded architecture. The chamber behind the cards becomes quieter and darker with less competing detail; retain the suggestion of the window, arches and oak table. Remove the decorative side wall banner, foreground book stack and loose map clutter. Use quieter empty space in their existing places. This is authored painterly game art with focus, not a blur filter.

SIMPLIFY THE UI TO MATCH THE CURRENT FALL DESIGN SYSTEM:
Functional UI is crisp and mostly flat, warm near-black/charcoal surfaces, warm off-white text, thin muted bronze borders. Existing fonts are Cinzel headings and Spline Sans body. Approximate those faithfully: moderately weighted Cinzel labels, clean Spline Sans-like functional text, good kerning, avoid thin oversized Roman lettering and ornate italic captions.
1. The three card frames become refined thin bronze single/double rules on charcoal with only subtly clipped or softly rounded corners. REMOVE the repeated coin/sword/cup/clover corner ornaments, all filigree, the lion badge hanging from the centre card and thick bevelled gold mouldings. Keep the Campaign selected border slightly stronger and lighter, never luminous. Preserve a recognisable crafted game-card silhouette, not plain website panels.
2. Each card has a clean matte charcoal title band. Titles exactly "THE TAVERN", "CAMPAIGN", "ARENA", in restrained medium-weight Cinzel, smaller than the original but still prominent. Descriptions in readable nonitalic sans-serif: "A seat at the table", "The Borderlands", "Prove your hand". Replace the parchment chapter ribbon with a small simple text caption "CHAPTER II" near the Campaign title area, not laid over the main illustration on a scroll.
3. Primary action keeps the same footprint and position but becomes a SIMPLE solid crimson-red button, approximately the project's brand-red oklch(0.606046 0.223912 25.3317), with a fine quiet edge and small corner radius. Exact text "Continue campaign", clean medium-weight sans-serif. Remove gold bevels, leather texture, ornamental tips, internal flourishes and shadow stacks. One low-key arrow icon may sit at the right.
4. Keep "FALL" but make its wordmark cleaner and modestly smaller; REMOVE the oak-leaf flourish underneath.
5. Top-left profile: a simpler thin bronze circular portrait ring, name "Traveller" and small "Level 12" in clean sans-serif. Top-right: a small consistent thin-line coin symbol, "1,240", simple envelope and gear, no heavy decorative dividers.
6. Bottom navigation becomes a low-profile charcoal strip with five evenly spaced SMALL consistent thin-line icons (shield, stacked cards, open book, group of people, shop) and exact sans-serif labels "Hero", "Collection", "Journal", "Guild", "Market". Remove all realistic sculpted helmet/book/scales miniatures and floral corners. Icons and labels should look feasible using an existing Lucide-style icon library, with generous click areas.
7. Current-quest area: replace the large 3D quill and scroll with a modest thin-line journal icon and small sans-serif text "Current quest" and "A debt at the crossroads". The "All modes" secondary action should be simple sans-serif with a small chevron, maintaining its current location.

Quality: retain richness inside the activity paintings while simplifying everything that will become real UI components. Preserve breathing room and clear alignment. No bright gold glow, no dust particles, no candles, no new dramatic lighting, no flat website hero layout, no extra copy, no UI annotations. All text clean and readable. Make a disciplined iteration of this image, not a different concept.
refinements: Edit this exact FALL Card Hall menu mockup with only two precise corrections. 1) The small parchment chapter ribbon inside the centre Campaign card currently contains misspelled text. Replace its entire lettering with exactly 'CHAPTER II' — C H A P T E R, space, I I — clean readable dark serif lettering. Keep the same ribbon size and position. 2) Remove the white/yellow luminous halo around the centre card. Retain a clear selected state using a flat satin aged-brass double rim, slightly brighter than the side cards, with NO emitted light, bloom or glow. Preserve all three paintings, faces, composition, positions, card sizes, header, bottom navigation, text everywhere else, textures, natural lighting and overall quality exactly. Do not redesign or recompose the image. Output the same 16:9 full-screen menu.
